name: Convert
summary: Privacy-first A/B testing platform: experiments, personalization and feature rollouts, priced by tested users. Via our link: an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (standard is 15 days).
best_for: CRO teams running serious A/B and multivariate testing who want a privacy-first, GDPR-friendly alternative to the big experimentation suites
skip_if: your traffic is modest: statistical significance needs volume, and 100K tested users a month is more than most small sites can use, or your landing-page tool's built-in testing covers it
honest_knock: The meter is tested users, and it keeps running: blow past your monthly allowance and overuse blocks land at $399-699 unless you hard-cap them, and every extra custom domain is $1,000 a year. The friendly $299 headline assumes annual prepay; month-to-month is $399. One thing people misprice, and it is not the test itself: everyone expects an experiment to end when the subscription does. The trap is the winner. Convert describes itself as a client-side tool where “adding just one snippet of code on your site will then do all of the magic”. So a winning variant you leave running in the visual editor is not a change to your site: it is a rendering by their script. Ship the winner into your own code, or you are paying rent on a result you already bought.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month, or $299 a month billed annually ($3,588/yr)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-26 on convert.com/pricing: every plan name, amount, tested-user allowance, limit and overuse rate unchanged; the Growth card now also lists an MCP Server, and Convert Intelligence is marked beta on both cards; first re-verified 2026-09-20) 15-day standard free trial — through our link it's an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (verified 16 Jul 2026, no credit card). Growth $399/mo, or $299/mo paid annually ($3,588/yr, which the page calls a 25% saving); Pro $599/mo, or $420/mo paid annually ($5,040/yr, a 30% saving); Enterprise on request, annual only. Tested users are a slider rather than a plan feature: at the base position Growth AND Pro both include 100K tested users a month (1.2M a year), and Enterprise starts at 1M a month (12M a year). The tiers differ on limits — active projects 5 / 30 / unlimited, active experiences per project 5 / unlimited / unlimited, active domains 10 / unlimited / unlimited, goals per project 30 / 100 / 200, custom segments 5 / 10 / 20, deploys 10 / 100 / 300 — and Growth is marked absent on multipage, multivariate and full-stack testing, multi-arm bandit allocation, geotargeting, weather targeting, custom pop-ups and the beta request-approval system. Overuse is metered at $399 per extra 100K on Growth and $699 per 250K on Pro and Enterprise, and can be switched off; each additional custom domain (CNAME) costs $1,000/year. Prices exclude VAT and GST. Native heatmaps and frustration-sensing session recordings are included at every tier at no extra cost and do not consume tested users; 8% of the annual fee goes to tree planting with TIST.

claims.claim: I don't know whether my small traffic is enough for a reliable test.
claims.observed: A draft A/B experiment was ready in about 84 seconds, but the report tab only says it is too early to judge the experiment and shows the columns Confidence Level and Confidence Interval. No sample size calculator was found, and no traffic could be run.
claims.plan: Trial account on Pro 100k; a project and a draft A/B experiment on example.com were made without the snippet and the plans were read in the account and on the public pricing page; nothing was activated or bought
claims.comparability: The pain of the audience group against a draft that never had traffic; no calculation could be made.
claims.buying_consequence: The tool does not tell a small site up front whether its traffic is enough, so work that out with a separate calculator before you pay.

claims.claim: Convert snippet not detected on your site. Some features may be limited due to missing code or site restrictions.
claims.observed: The visual editor loaded example.com with this banner and a warning to install the Convert Chrome Extension. The change was still saved, and the experience was saved as a draft without the snippet or a verified domain.
claims.plan: Trial account on Pro 100k; a project and a draft A/B experiment on example.com were made without the snippet and the plans were read in the account and on the public pricing page; nothing was activated or bought
claims.comparability: The editor banner and the saved draft in our own session; the snippet was never installed.
claims.buying_consequence: You can build and save a test before the code is on your site, but you only find out what is limited when you install it.

claims.claim: Don't forget to install your project code into the header of your experience/goals pages.
claims.observed: The status menu offers Draft, Active and Scheduled and shows this reminder when it opens. The status was not set to Active, so nothing ran on any page.
claims.plan: Trial account on Pro 100k; a project and a draft A/B experiment on example.com were made without the snippet and the plans were read in the account and on the public pricing page; nothing was activated or bought
claims.comparability: The reminder in the status menu; no live page and no traffic were used.
claims.buying_consequence: Nothing is measured until the code sits in the header of every page of the test.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session set up a Convert trial, made a project on example.com and saved a draft A/B experiment with one changed heading, all in about 84 seconds from 18:36:01 to 18:37:25, without installing the code snippet or verifying the domain (the editor only warns that the snippet was not detected). The report tab says it is too early to judge and the tool has no sample size calculator, so the question of a team with small traffic cannot be answered before a test has run. The trial shows the Pro 100k plan with 100K tested users a month, 14 days left, no payment method and Over Quota charges: Allowed. The prices match the dossier (Growth 399 dollars a month or 299 dollars billed annually, Pro 599 or 420), but this account got the standard 15-day trial and the 30-day trial of the dossier through our link was not seen, because the account was not made through that link. Nothing was activated, bought or cancelled. Account and start: we created the account (a trial of Convert Experiences) and our AI assistant worked in its own tab of his browser from 18:36:01 (Amsterdam). The interface was already in English. The start screen offered What's Next with Explore Demo Project and Create a New Project, and a notice about an extra layer of security: You have 14 days left. After that, you'll need to set up 2FA before making changes. Remind me later was chosen, so no 2FA was set up. The dossier name is Convert and the review is on AIBM (the b2b section, review page of Convert). Audience: the request named Teams running their first A/B tests (pain: I do not know whether my small traffic is enough for a reliable test). The dossier groups are different (CRO teams, multivariate and geotargeting, data residency in the EU); the best fit is CRO teams running steady A/B test programs, with tested users as the meter. Core action: Create a New Project, name Test Project, domain example.com (Web, standard privacy ticks), message Project Test Project has been created successfully!, and straight after it Install the Code Snippet on Your Website; the script was NOT placed. Then a new experience Headline test, URL example.com, type A/B. The visual editor loads example.com with a banner that the Convert snippet was not detected on the site, and the advice to install the Convert Chrome Extension (nothing was installed). The heading of the page was replaced through Edit, Text with Start your free test today and Save Element Changes; the change is listed as Changed Text. Summary: status Draft, split Original Page 50% and Variation 1 50%, goals Decrease BounceRate (Primary Goal) and Increase Engagement (standard). Saving worked without the snippet and without a verified domain. The status menu offers Draft, Active and Scheduled, and opening it says Do not forget to install your project code into the header of your experience/goals pages. The status was not set to Active. Time: start 18:36:01, concept ready at 18:37:25, so about 84 seconds and 9 to 10 steps. Report tab: It's too early to judge this experiment, with the columns Confidence Level and Confidence Interval; there is no sample size calculator, so the question whether small traffic is enough for a reliable test cannot be answered inside the tool before a test has traffic. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in the account (Account Settings, Plans) and on convert.com/pricing; prices exclude VAT and GST and taxes are added at checkout. Monthly view in the app: Growth 100k 399 dollars a month, Pro 100k 599 dollars (marked Current Trial Plan), Growth 250k 799, Pro 250k 999, Growth 500k 1,499, Pro 500k 1,899, Growth 750k 2,199, Pro 750k 2,799, Pro 1M 3,699, Pro 1.5M 4,238, Pro 2M 4,982; Enterprise starts at 3M unique tested users a month. Nexus (Deploy): Basic 99 dollars (1K visitor profiles), Pro 399, Enterprise 1,999. Annual view (SAVE 30%): Growth 1.2M yearly 299 dollars a month (3,588 a year), Pro 1.2M yearly 420 dollars a month (5,040 a year), Growth 3M yearly 560 dollars a month (6,720 a year). Growth has 5 Tests and 5 Active Projects; Pro has Unlimited Tests and 30 Active Projects. The public page says Starting 299 dollars a month (paid annually) or 399 dollars a month (paid monthly), offers Start 15-Day Free Trial with No Credit Card Required and has a slider from 100K a month up; the Pro list names Sequential Testing: Call tests faster while controlling for false positives. Trial in the account: Current Plan Pro 100k, You are in the Free Trial, the trial ends in 14 days (Next Payment Date December 3, 2026), 100K tested users a month, Payment Method None, Over Quota charges: Allowed. There was no card field and nothing was filled in, so no checkout total, tax or fee line was seen. The prices match the dossier; this delivery does not change them. Deviations from the dossier: (1) the dossier names an exclusive 30-day trial through our link; this account was not made through our link and got 15 days, so the 30 days were not seen. (2) The dossier says tested users are a slider; in the account they are separate plans (Growth 100k, Pro 100k and so on), while the public page has a slider. (3) The dossier says Enterprise starts at 1M tested users a month; the account says 3M a month. (4) The account is on Over Quota charges: Allowed; the dossier says overuse can be switched off, which was not tried. Cancelling: on Name and Billing the line Next Payment Date has a link Cancel; it was not clicked and the account was not deleted. Not tested: starting the test (Active), a snippet on a real site, 2FA, the Chrome extension, a sample size calculation (no traffic), the counting of tested users, overuse settings and any payment. Clean up (still so): the account, the project Test Project and the experience Headline test (Draft) stay; our tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The experience can be saved and set up without the snippet or a verified domain, but nothing runs until the code is in the header of the pages, and the editor only warns about it in a banner. The tool has no sample size calculator, and the report says it is too early to judge before there is traffic. The account is on Over Quota charges: Allowed from the start of the trial. In the account the tested users are separate plans, while the public page has a slider, and the annual switch says SAVE 30% although the saving on Growth is smaller. The trial of this account was 15 days and the 30-day trial through our link was not given.

A sample size calculation, which needs traffic.
The counting of tested users and the overuse settings.

Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.
